title: On Error Correction for Nonvolatile Processing-In-Memory
problem: Nonvolatile PiM systems inherit memory substrate vulnerabilities and introduce computation-induced errors, yet existing error correcting codes typically ignore errors during computation. Error correction must address both storage and computation-induced errors.
motivation: Processing-in-memory offers significant energy efficiency for data-intensive applications, but reliability concerns must be resolved for practical deployment.
method: The paper surveys the error correction design space for nonvolatile PiM, comparing self-checking and homomorphic approaches. Multiple solutions are proposed that guarantee single error correction for both bulk bitwise computations and memory errors, with performance-area-coverage trade-off analysis across three representative nonvolatile PiM technologies.
key_novelty: Holistic error correction approach for nonvolatile PiM that simultaneously handles both memory substrate errors and computation-induced errors using self-checking and homomorphic techniques.
contributions: Survey of error correction design space for nonvolatile PiM addressing both storage and computation-induced errors
Proposed solutions guaranteeing single error correction for bitwise computations and memory errors
Performance-area-coverage trade-off analysis across three representative nonvolatile PiM technologies
Comparison of self-checking and homomorphic error correction approaches

metrics.accuracy: single error correction for memory and computation errors
